recap:
## Decisions
- The prototype is feasible from both production and marketing points of view. It is snail-shaped, has a blue plastic case and soft rubber buttons in several colours, and comes with a shell-shaped holder. [00:31:16]
- Buttons will show numbers and symbols, and text will be printed on the case, so nothing is language-dependent. [00:12:37]
- The marketing campaign will push two selling points: the look (snail image) and voice recognition. [00:14:00]
- The components are a battery, a simple chip on print, a double-curved plastic case with special colours, and push buttons with special colour, form and material. There is no LCD display. [00:17:02]
- The estimated cost of €8.20 is well within budget. [00:17:33]
- The team rated shape 1 and colour 1 (1 is best, 7 is worst). [00:25:34]

## Action items
- owner not assigned: Show the prototype to people from various age and socio-economic groups, and to consumer research groups, to fine-tune it and check safety. [00:19:32]

## Unresolved
- The voice recogniser was not included in the financing. It is unclear whether the remaining ~€4.30 will cover it. [00:22:46]
- Speech recognition will need extra buttons. Ideas included dropping one mute button, putting volume on one button, and using smaller buttons, but none was settled. [00:28:29]
- Functionality was rated lowest (2–3), and another meeting may be needed. [00:26:41]
- Size ratings differed: ME gave 4, PM gave 2, and UI and ID gave 1. [00:25:11]
